sections.html:
Rockville is the county seat of Montgomery County, in the Piedmont region and part of the Washington metropolitan area. The population was 61,209 in 2010 and 67,117 in 2020. Rock Creek, Cabin John Creek and Watts Branch cross the city, so ask about drainage if your lot sits low.

Growth came in layers, so parts of the city look older than others. Older blocks near the courthouse and in districts such as Rockville Park and West Montgomery Avenue sit beside mid-century subdivisions like Twinbrook and newer planned areas. Name the part of town when you describe the house. Because Rockville is a city inside a county, a house here answers to two sets of rules and two tax levies.

sections.h2: Property tax and the county bill
sections.html:
One consolidated Montgomery County bill carries the city's tax. Assessed values come from the State Department of Assessments and Taxation, and bills go out in July.

Fiscal 2026 chargeRate per $100 of assessed value
County rate0.7212
City of Rockville rate0.2920
Special rate0.2056
Total1.2188

Rockville adds its own supplement to the Homeowners' Property Tax Credit. To qualify, a household needs gross income of $91,000 or less and net worth under $200,000 (the home and qualified retirement savings do not count). It applies to the first $495,000 of assessed value. Call city Finance at 240-314-8400.

Each property is reassessed every three years, with any increase spread equally across the three. You can appeal within 45 days of the notice date.

  1. Start with the local assessment office.
  2. Still unhappy? Take it to the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board within 30 days of the final notice.
  3. The final stop is the Maryland Tax Court, which must hear it within 30 days of the board's order.

Even with a sale coming up, an appeal is worth a look: the assessment feeds the tax split on your settlement sheet.

County transfer and recordation taxes belong on your list for the settlement company. The residential transfer tax in Montgomery County ranges from 0.25% to 1% depending on the sale price. The recordation tax has a first $100,000 exemption for a buyer's principal residence, plus extra tiered amounts above $500,000.

Unpaid bills can end up in the county's real property tax lien sale. With back taxes in the picture, either clear them yourself or let the title company settle them out of your proceeds.

A single-family rental in Rockville, whether a detached house, townhome or condominium, needs a Rental Property License to open or renew. The Community Planning and Development Services Department administers the licenses.

Tenants in the house you want to sell? Confirm the license is up to date before you list. The department can explain any inspection requirement and tell you if something is open that might hold up closing.

Owners inside a locally designated historic district must get a Certificate of Approval from the Historic District Commission before changing the exterior. The commission sits on the third Thursday of every month at 7 p.m.

  • Work that needs review includes additions, demolition, window and door changes, roofing and siding changes, fences, driveways and major tree removal.
  • Staff can approve some minor work, such as accessory structures up to 150 square feet.
  • The city aims to schedule review within 45 days of accepting an application, and an approved project must be finished within five years.
  • Building and use permits are separate from the Certificate of Approval.

Many National Register properties are listed, including the Beall-Dawson House, Old St. Mary's Church and the Rockville Railroad Station. National listing and local designation are separate, so ask the city which applies to your address.

The Metro Red Line stops at Rockville and Twinbrook stations, both opened in 1984, and MARC's Brunswick Line serves Rockville Station on the way to Washington Union Station. Amtrak also runs from Rockville to Chicago and Washington. I-270 is the main highway, Maryland Route 355 (Rockville Pike) is the main commercial road, and Ride On provides local bus service. Say plainly how far the house is from the Red Line, since buyers can look that up too.

Repeated freezing and thawing plus long humid stretches wear on roofs, gutters, attic ventilation and basements. Rockville gets about 40.3 inches of precipitation and roughly 17.1 inches of snow in a typical year. These are reasonable items to check before a sale. A buyer's inspector will look at the same places, so a quick look by a roofer or handyman beforehand can head off a price cut. If you skip repairs, a cash buyer will usually take the house as it is and price the work in.

sections.h2: Disclosure and what a cash sale skips
sections.html:
Maryland expects a seller of a one-to-four unit home to give the buyer a disclosure or disclaimer form before signing. A cash purchase has no lender behind it, which removes the appraisal and loan underwriting steps, though an inspection and title search can still happen.

For a Rockville house with a tenant, an open historic review or back taxes, that means the closing date depends on how quickly those items are settled, not on a bank.

• The latest consolidated tax bill and your assessment notice.
  • The rental license and any inspection record, if the house is leased.
  • Any Certificate of Approval for past exterior work in a historic district.
  • A list of repairs you know about, so the disclosure form is accurate.

A buyer who sees complete paperwork makes a cleaner offer, and you spend less time answering follow-up questions by phone or email. The settlement company will ask for most of these anyway, so gathering them first saves days later.

Ask the city Finance Department and the county for the exact payoff before you accept an offer, because the tax balance sets the minimum your sale must cover. A cash sale skips lender underwriting, so once the payoff is confirmed the title company can usually give you a clear closing date. Save any notice that arrives during the contract period.

For an inherited house, bring proof of who may sell it. With several heirs, delays usually come from signatures rather than price, so line up everyone who has to sign.

1. Find out if the house sits in a historic district and if the rental license is up to date.
  2. Get the tax balance from the county or city Finance.
  3. Fill out the disclosure or disclaimer form.
  4. Ask the settlement company what transfer and recordation will cost.
  5. Sign at closing while taxes and liens are paid out of your proceeds.

faqs.q: Is Rockville the Montgomery County seat?
faqs.a: Yes, and it has held that role since the county was created in 1776.

faqs.q: Who bills property tax in Rockville?
faqs.a: Montgomery County sends a single bill that already includes the city's $0.292 per $100. It arrives in July. Assessed values are set by the state.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Rockville property assessment?
faqs.a: The clock is 45 days from the date printed on the reassessment notice. Three levels follow in order: the local assessment office, the Appeals Board, then Tax Court, each with a 30-day window after the one before.

faqs.q: Do I need city approval to change the outside of a historic Rockville house?
faqs.a: Yes, when the address sits in a locally designated district. The Historic District Commission reviews roofing, siding, windows, fences and driveways, and holds its meetings the third Thursday monthly.

faqs.q: Does Rockville require a license to rent a single-family house?
faqs.a: Yes. Detached houses, townhomes and condominiums rented out in the city all need a Rental Property License. The city's planning department supplies the application.
